nodes.description: A heterozygous activating AKT3 variant, either constitutional (de novo or inherited from a mosaic parent) or post-zygotic. All tested variants raise AKT3 kinase activity; variants in the pleckstrin homology (PH) domain, such as p.E17K, additionally increase binding to membrane phosphoinositides, the step that recruits AKT to the membrane for activation. Strongly activating variants tend to be tolerated only as low-level mosaics and produce focal malformations, while milder constitutional variants produce diffuse megalencephaly.

nodes.description: AKT3 is the most abundant AKT paralog in the developing cortex, and phosphorylated AKT is concentrated in dividing radial glial progenitors of the ventricular zone. Activated AKT3 increases signalling through mTORC1, seen in patient brain as increased phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6. Because the progenitors give rise to both neurons and glia, a variant arising in them is inherited by the cortical lineages they produce.
